findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the DC description convergence test must inject ALL THREE of outbound_mapper=, inbound_mapper=, and links= (or pass a fully-constructed DC backend instance) to prevent compute_outbound_mutations:431's OR condition from invoking select_backend(load_config()) for the uninjected members.
evidence: outbound_differ.py:431: 'if outbound_mapper is None or inbound_mapper is None or links is None:' — OR means injecting only one still triggers the block
Plan text: 'DESCRIPTION convergence: drive compute_outbound_mutations with an explicit outbound_mapper= bound to DC's mapper, never relying on the fallback'
AC5: 'the description test injects outbound_mapper= explicitly; neither relies on select_backend(load_config())'
Links is also resolved from the backend and is used for link-diff logic; inbound_mapper affects normalize_rich_text on the remote description value
findings.finding: The description convergence test shape prescribed by the plan — 'drive compute_outbound_mutations with an explicit outbound_mapper= bound to DC's mapper' — is insufficient to prevent the Cloud-backend fallback. compute_outbound_mutations:431 uses an OR condition: if outbound_mapper is None OR inbound_mapper is None OR links is None, select_backend(load_config()) is called and ALL missing members are filled from Cloud. A test injecting only outbound_mapper= still leaves inbound_mapper=None and links=None, which triggers the Cloud fallback for those two. AC5 ('neither relies on select_backend(load_config())') and AC6 (mutation-check: removing the injection turns the cell red) are both unmet if only outbound_mapper= is injected — unless the test also injects inbound_mapper= and links= (or supplies a DC backend instance covering all three).
findings.location: Approach step 3 / 'DESCRIPTION convergence' bullet; AC5; AC6; outbound_differ.py:431-441
scenarios: A developer writes the DC description convergence test injecting only outbound_mapper=. The OR condition fires, Cloud's inbound_mapper and links are used. For plain-text DC bodies, Cloud's normalize_rich_text passes strings through unchanged (dict-guard), so the test passes — but is exercising Cloud's inbound path, not DC's. AC6 mutation test (remove injection → red) may also pass vacuously if Cloud's outbound_mapper also truncates at 32767.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach section's DESCRIPTION convergence bullet, change 'drive compute_outbound_mutations with an explicit outbound_mapper= bound to DC's mapper' to 'drive compute_outbound_mutations with explicit outbound_mapper=, inbound_mapper=, and links= all bound to DC instances (or pass a constructed JiraDataCenterBackend), so the OR guard at outbound_differ.py:431 cannot fall back to select_backend(load_config()) for any member'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Revise the comment convergence test's discriminating strategy: since DC's and Cloud's comment truncation produce identical output at 32767 chars, prove DC injection by asserting on a property that DIFFERS between backends (e.g. use a spy/mock sanitizer that records calls, or assert that the truncation function object is `WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound` not `comment_limits.truncate_comment_body`), and update the mutation-check AC to reflect the correct discriminant.
evidence: DC `_DCSanitizer.fit_comment` → `WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound`: truncates at `WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` (32767) with suffix `_WIKI_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX = ' … [truncated by reconciler]'` (rich_text.py:69,93-94)

Cloud `_JiraSanitizer.fit_comment` → `comment_limits.truncate_comment_body`: truncates at `_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS` (32767) with suffix `_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX = ' … [truncated by reconciler]'` (comment_limits.py:41,46,69-70)
Both limits are 32767 and both suffixes are the identical string — the outputs are byte-for-byte equal

Plan AC4: 'Cloud's is an ADF-serialized fit at _ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT (32000) and CANNOT produce that result' — this is true for descriptions but not comments; the plan conflates the description-vs-comment distinction it correctly identifies elsewhere
findings.finding: The discriminating assertion and mutation-check AC for the comment test are unachievable as specified: DC's `fit_comment` (`WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound`, 32767 chars, suffix `' … [truncated by reconciler]'`) and Cloud's `fit_comment` (`comment_limits.truncate_comment_body`, 32767 chars, IDENTICAL suffix) produce byte-for-byte identical output for any input. No assertion on the truncated body can distinguish the two, so removing the `sanitizer=` injection (the required mutation check) leaves the test green — exactly the vacuous-green the plan claims to eliminate.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria: 'each DC convergence test PROVES it exercised DC's truncation and not Cloud's, by a DISCRIMINATING assertion' and 'REMOVING the explicit injection...turns the DC cells RED'; also 'DC path is a plain-character fit at WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT ending in the wiki truncation suffix; Cloud's is an ADF-serialized fit at _ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT (32000) and CANNOT produce that result' — this characterisation is correct for DESCRIPTIONS but WRONG for COMMENTS.
scenarios: Implementer writes the DC comment convergence test with a correct `sanitizer=` injection and a length/suffix assertion. Test is green. Implementer then removes the injection for the mutation check — Cloud's sanitizer is used instead, produces the identical 32767-char suffix-terminated string, and the test stays green. The mutation check passes vacuously, the AC is claimed satisfied, and the test proves nothing about which backend was exercised.
Any future drift (e.g. one suffix string changes) would silently break the mutation-check guarantee with no test catching it.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the length/suffix discriminating assertion with an identity check on the injected sanitizer: capture the DC sanitizer instance, assert `sanitizer.fit_comment is dc_backend.sanitizer.fit_comment` (or use a recording wrapper), and for the mutation-check show that omitting the injection causes the wrapper NOT to be called. Alternatively, construct a synthetic DC sanitizer with a DELIBERATELY DIFFERENT suffix (e.g. `'[DC-truncated]'`) purely for test discrimination — making the two backends produce distinguishably different output — and assert on that suffix.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the description convergence test also injects `inbound_mapper=dc_backend.inbound` and `links=dc_backend` (or explicit stubs) into `compute_outbound_mutations`, so NONE of the three optional slots trigger the `select_backend(load_config())` fallback, fully satisfying AC5.
evidence: `compute_outbound_mutations` signature has `outbound_mapper`, `inbound_mapper`, and `links` as separate optional kwargs (outbound_differ.py:388-390)

Line 431: `if outbound_mapper is None or inbound_mapper is None or links is None:` — if only `outbound_mapper` is supplied, the condition is still True and the fallback fires, resolving `inbound_mapper` and `links` from `load_config()`
AC5 states 'neither relies on `select_backend(load_config())`' — but injecting only `outbound_mapper` still triggers the fallback for the other two slots
findings.finding: The description convergence test, as specified (inject only `outbound_mapper=`), still invokes `select_backend(load_config())` for `inbound_mapper` and `links`, because `compute_outbound_mutations` at line 431 uses an OR-guard: if any of the three is `None`, the fallback block fires and resolves all three from config. This partially contradicts AC5 ('neither relies on `select_backend(load_config())`').
findings.location: Approach section step 3 ('DESCRIPTION convergence: drive `compute_outbound_mutations` with an explicit `outbound_mapper=` bound to DC's mapper, never relying on the fallback'); outbound_differ.py:431-441; AC5.
scenarios: The description test injects `outbound_mapper=dc_backend.outbound` only. The fallback block at line 431 fires because `inbound_mapper is None`. `load_config()` is called and resolves a Cloud backend's `inbound_mapper`. For DC-shaped snapshots (plain-string bodies) this is functionally harmless (Cloud's `normalize_rich_text` passes plain strings through unchanged). But the test has silently called `load_config()` in violation of its own AC, and in a test environment where config is misconfigured this causes an unrelated failure.

The mutation check becomes ambiguous: removing `outbound_mapper=` causes the fallback to supply Cloud's outbound mapper — but the test already relied on the fallback for `inbound_mapper` and `links`, so the mutation was never fully isolated.
findings.suggested_fix: In the description test: `compute_outbound_mutations(..., outbound_mapper=dc_backend.outbound, inbound_mapper=dc_backend.inbound, links=dc_backend)`. Construct a minimal `JiraDataCenterBackend` with a stub transport for test purposes.

findings.finding: The leaf's file_impact metadata lists the *existing* Cloud convergence test files (`test_outbound_comment_length_convergence.py` and `test_outbound_description_length_convergence.py`) as the paths to be changed, with reason 'extend Cloud comment-convergence coverage to DC (two-pass property)' and 'extend Cloud description-convergence coverage to DC (two-pass property)'. 'mutation-checked: raising the limit above the real ceiling, or removing the fit, turns a convergence test red'
Neither AC names a test runner command or describes how the mutation is recorded in the PR
findings.finding: The two mutation-check ACs ('REMOVING the explicit injection turns the DC cells RED' and 'raising the limit above the real ceiling, or removing the fit, turns a convergence test red') are stated as done-conditions but carry no proving command — no `pytest` invocation, no specification of which line to mutate. An executor has no concrete evidence protocol to satisfy these ACs, and a reviewer cannot verify them from a PR alone.

findings.finding: The plan specifies that DC convergence tests exercise `WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound` (DC's truncation path), but `compute_outbound_mutations` falls back to `select_backend(load_config())` when `outbound_mapper`/`inbound_mapper` are not explicitly injected, and `outbound_comments._resolve_sanitizer` does the same. If the test environment's configured backend is Cloud (the existing default), the DC tests would inadvertently exercise Cloud's ADF truncation path rather than DC's `WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound`, making the convergence assertion vacuously pass against the wrong truncation function.

The DC comment convergence test cannot exercise DC's sanitizer path through the standard compute_outbound_mutations injection seam. _diff_comments resolves its sanitizer via _resolve_sanitizer(None) → select_backend(load_config()).sanitizer — independently of the outbound_mapper/inbound_mapper the test injects — so the test would silently call Cloud's fit_comment (or fail on config load) rather than DC's WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound for the comment-body membership comparison. A test that converges via the wrong backend's sanitizer is not establishing DC convergence.
findings.location: Approach section, item 2 / outbound_comments.py:_diff_comments (line 205: _resolve_sanitizer(sanitizer)) / outbound_differ.py:744 (_diff_comments called without sanitizer=)
